subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` session archive convention plus physical archive cleanup behavior with a permanent archive naming or directory model, and what migration/purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current behavior, but choosing new filenames, directory layout, deletion policy, and compatibility semantics changes shipped storage contracts and downstream operator tooling.

options.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind explicit documented retention controls.

options.title: Keep behavior and clarify docs
options.body: Leave current suffixes and cleanup behavior intact, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk budget removes it.

options.title: Split naming from purge policy
options.body: Use the open semantics issue for suffix/config clarity while tracking no-physical-delete as a separate data durability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind explicit documented retention controls.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session management and docs work makes this the strongest available owner for choosing the user-facing lifecycle contract.
